title: Fill a blood tube on a needle already in a training arm's vein and take it off without moving the needle
instruction: On the practice arm, fill the blood tube, then lay it in the tray.
context: Drawing blood by vacuum tube is core work for medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092: 'Collect blood, tissue, or other laboratory specimens, log the specimens, and prepare them for testing'; 833,900 US jobs, BLS 2025) and for phlebotomists (31-9097: 'Draw blood from veins by vacuum tube, syringe, or butterfly venipuncture methods'; 143,900). In a multi-tube draw the needle stays in the vein while each tube is pushed onto the holder's back needle, filled and pulled off; here one tube is filled and taken off on a practice arm, the needle already placed. Training manuals warn that if the holder is not held steady while the tube is pushed in, the needle may 'slip out of the vein' or 'puncture the opposing vein wall', and the holder must be stabilised while the tube is pulled off. Pushing or pulling on the tube alone moves the needle. Unlike drawing a syringe's plunger while its needle sits in a vial's stopper, here the needle is in tissue and the tube itself is forced onto and off it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the table. Training arm: an adult venipuncture training arm (skin-tone vinyl over a rigid core), 80 cm shoulder to fingertips, lying palm up along y at x 25, shoulder to the left (y +42), fingertips at y -38, fixed to the table; upper arm 9.6 cm wide, forearm 8.4 cm, skin over the elbow crease 6 cm up, a blue vein along its top. In the vein at the crease (x 25, y 6): a 21G x 1 inch multi-sample needle (green hub) entering at 25 deg and pointing up the arm, 9 mm in (tip 3.8 mm under the skin). On it: a single-use clear polypropylene tube holder, 19 mm across, 48 mm long, 17 mm bore, finger flange 34 x 24 x 2 mm at its open end (long side turned 40 deg from vertical toward the robot), the back needle in its rubber sleeve inside. In the holder: a 13 x 75 mm, 4 mL no-additive evacuated glass tube with a red rubber stopper (81 mm overall, 7 g), pushed in to the guide line only (stopper touching the sleeve, not pierced), 44 mm of it out past the flange. Tray: white plastic, 9.8 x 11 x 1.2 cm, two open slots 4 x 9.8 cm (4 mm floor), centred at x 42, y -13. Arms start in the ready pose.
scoring: Latched 0 for the trial if, at any moment from the start to the end of the trial (before, during and after the fill, while the tube is pulled off and after): (1) the needle moved more than 2 mm along its line from its start, either way (out of the vein's lumen); (2) the needle's hub moved more than 2 mm sideways, in any direction across the needle's start line (about the radius of the cubital vein, 3.9-4.8 mm across); (3) the needle pivoted more than 3 deg from its start direction, in any direction (spin about its own axis is not counted); (4) the holder was let go of after it was first held (no hand on it for 0.25 s); or (5) the stopper was never pierced. Sim: (1) from the needle's slide, (2) and (3) from the holder's pose every physics step (the sim's needle can only slide, so they cannot trip there). Real rig, on video: a pen mark on the skin at the hub, a paint dot on the green hub, and two fixed cameras, 30 fps or more, each 20 cm from the hub's face and looking along a normal to the needle: a side camera beyond the training arm, lens at x 45, y 4.55, 6.7 cm up, looking toward the robot (-x); and an overhead camera, lens at x 25, y 13.0, 24.8 cm up, aimed down at the hub along the needle's upward normal (tilted 25 deg from vertical toward the shoulder, square to the needle); the mm scale in each view is the holder barrel's 19 mm width. On the last frame before the robot first touches anything, overlay the needle's start line (the barrel's axis) and the hub dot in each view. In any later frame (read every 5th frame, and frame by frame wherever the holder visibly moves; where a gripper blocks a camera's view of the hub dot or barrel, use that camera's nearest unblocked frame within 0.5 s, and if there is none that interval fails, latched 0), latched for (1) if the hub-to-mark gap along the needle, 16.4 mm at the start (1 inch needle, 9 mm in), is under 14.4 or over 18.4 mm; for (2) if the hub dot is more than 2 mm from the start line, combined from the two views (square root of the sum of the squares); for (3) if the barrel's axis, read along at least 20 mm of its visible edge, has turned from the start line by more than 3 deg, combined the same way (1.05 mm across per 20 mm along). Otherwise: 0.25 the stopper pierced with the needle in the vein; 0.5 the tube filled to its fill mark (at least 90 % of 4 mL; on a real training arm the artificial blood comes only from the vein); 0.75 that and the tube off the needle and out of the holder; 1.0 that and the tube lying in a tray slot (wholly inside it, on its floor), let go (no gripper within 2.5 cm) and still, with the holder still held. Success when 1.0 holds for 1 s; otherwise scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Set the needle back to its start mark (9 mm in), replace the tube with a fresh evacuated one (a filled or pierced tube has no vacuum left) pushed into the holder to the guide line only, and empty the tray. The needle is sharp: keep people clear of the training arm while the robot works.
fidelity: Full-size rigid parts; holder/tube mu 0.3. Needle: a slide on its line in the arm, 0.5 N drag, lumen +-2 mm. So the sim constrains the needle to axial motion and cannot show sideways or pivot failures; those are checked in the real trial. Tube slides on that line: held at the guide line until a 4 N push pierces the stopper, then up to 1.5 N drag (0.3 N in the bore) to a stop 8 mm in; drags yield only to a finger's load. Fill: a counter, 4 mL in 8 s, only while pierced and in vein. Refs: README.
